jsDoc.doc:
Wrapper around a single media file and its EXIF metadata.

File objects are read-only until a setter is called. Setters accumulate
pending exiftool tag values in a Map; call {@link write} to apply them via
exiftool in one subprocess invocation. The Map structure is extensible and
supports arbitrary tags (GPS, location, etc.) through {@link setTag}.

Read JSON metadata from the file via exiftool.

Dates are read in canonical EXIF form (`YYYY:MM:DD HH:MM:SS`) so that
missing timezones can be distinguished from explicit UTC offsets.
Construct a File from pre-loaded metadata .

Return the full structured info object for this file. Includes all
populated sections (file, image, video, audio, doc, camera, app, gps).

tags.name: opts.metadata
tags.doc: Set to true to include the raw {@link Metadata} object.

jsDoc.doc: Converts decimal coordinates into the exact tag-value record needed by ExifTool.
The binary MakerNote block for the file, when present.

Queue an arbitrary exiftool tag write.

Pass `undefined` as the value to delete the tag. This is the extension
point for GPS, location, keywords, or any other tag not covered by the
typed setters.

Merge a changeset (tag→value map) from {@link Meta.Resolver} into the
pending tag buffer. Empty-string values delete the corresponding tag.

Apply all pending changes to the file via exiftool.

This is a no-op when nothing is dirty. After a successful write the dirty
flag is cleared, pending tags are dropped, and cached metadata is
invalidated.

Repair missing or corrupted date metadata for files whose source platform
stripped the embedded dates (e.g. TikTok, WhatsApp).

Uses the filesystem modified/created timestamp as the replacement date.
When the file was created with a dry-run flag, the changeset is computed
and queued but the exiftool write is a no-op.

tags.doc: true when a repair changeset was applied (or queued in dry-run).

jsDoc.doc:
The detected originator of a media file.

- `'camera'` — captured by a physical camera (Make/Model tags present; see
  the `camera` section of `info()` for device details).
- `'tiktok'` — downloaded from TikTok (metadata was stripped/replaced).
- `'whatsapp'` — shared via WhatsApp (metadata was stripped).
- `undefined` — origin could not be determined.
Read JSON metadata for one or more files.

tags.doc: An array of {@link File} instances, one per input file (in input order).

jsDoc.doc: EXIF date/time as emitted by exiftool (default format), e.g. "2026:07:31 18:00:00".

A GPS coordinate as emitted by exiftool.
Default (`-j` without `-n`): a DMS string with the reference embedded,
e.g. `"51 deg 30' 26.00" N"`. With `-n`: a decimal number of degrees.

Latitude/longitude reference hemisphere. exiftool emits the long form by
default (`"North"`) and the short form with `-n` (`"N"`).

Core EXIF and filesystem metadata tags.
Covers file info, image properties, camera/capture settings, dates,
GPS coordinates, thumbnails, and maker notes.
Directory path (string) or structured container info for JPEG with gain map
Byte ordering: "Little-endian (Intel, II)" or "Big-endian (Motorola, MM)"

Video duration. Default format is a string with units, e.g. `"2.00 s"`,
or `"H:MM:SS"`; with `-n` it is a plain number of seconds.
Altitude in meters; string form includes units, e.g. "192 m Above Sea Level".
0 = above sea level, 1 = below.
IPTC-IIM metadata tags (the older binary IPTC format, not XMP-based IPTC).
ICC color profile information embedded in the image.

XMP (Extensible Metadata Platform) tags.
These are typically written by Adobe products and other XMP-aware tools.
XMP edit history entries

Adobe Camera Raw / Lightroom develop settings (XMP `crs:` namespace).
These describe non-destructive raw processing adjustments. Present in any
image edited with Adobe Camera Raw, Lightroom, or Photoshop.

Exiftool composite (calculated) fields.
These are not stored directly but are derived by exiftool from other tags.
Video and audio codec/stream metadata.
QuickTime Keys atom creation date (e.g. "2024:10:29 18:43:30-06:00")
QuickTime track creation date
QuickTime media creation date
QuickTime track modification date
QuickTime media modification date
Free-form comment. TikTok writes a content ID here, e.g. "vid:v15044gf...".
Encoder software string, e.g. "Lavf58.76.100" (FFmpeg libavformat).
TikTok AI-generated-content info JSON, e.g. '{"aigc_label_type":0}'.

PDF metadata.
These tags are emitted by exiftool for non-media documents.
May be a string or, for some formats, an array of strings.
PDF producer application, e.g. "Adobe PDF Library 17.0".
Page count (PDF).
Page count (Office documents).
PDF version, e.g. "1.7".

Document metadata (PDF, Office, EPUB, text, etc.).
These tags are emitted by exiftool for non-media documents.
May be a string or, for some formats, an array of strings.
PDF producer application, e.g. "Adobe PDF Library 17.0".
Page count (PDF).
Page count (Office documents).
PDF version, e.g. "1.7".

The complete JSON object exiftool emits for one file with `-j`.
Fields are the raw tag names as produced by exiftool. Extends all
domain-specific metadata interfaces for a unified view.
Options shared by the {@link Reader} and {@link File} classes.
Compute and include a digest in the top-level file object.
Options when retrieving metadata from exiftools
On subsequent calls will use a cache version, unless set to true.
Options to File.info() method.
Include a top-level metadata object with the raw exiftool metadata
Compute and include a digest in the top-level file object.

JSON representation of a File's extracted metadata, nested by section.
Raw exiftool metadata is excluded by default; opt in with
`toJSON({ includeMetadata: true })`.
Options for {@link File.toJSON}.
A JSON-safe value (no Date, no undefined, etc.).

A single property definition in a section const.

`value` is the primary extractor; `json` is the JSON-serializable variant
(e.g. DateTime → ISO string). `title` overrides the auto-generated display
label; `asTitle` formats the value for display (defaults to `String(v)`).
A section is a name→InfoDef record.
The result object type for a section: all keys optional (undefined dropped).

Factory: read a raw EXIF tag value from the metadata object.
Covers the task's "1b: simpler case — just take a named property from metadata"
and "1c: take focalLength and get metadata.FocalLength".

Enumerate a section's defs and collect property values into a result object.
Keys are visited in declaration order. Properties whose value is `undefined`
are omitted (per task 1e). In `json` mode, each def's `json` extractor is
used when present; otherwise `value` is used as a fallback.

Display label for a key. Defaults to a title-cased version of the camelCase
key (e.g. `createdAt` → `Created At`). Override via the `title` field on
the InfoDef.

Filesystem-level information from {@link @epdoc/fs!FS.File} stats (not EXIF).
Returns `undefined` when the file's stats have not been read yet.
The last known software that processed/edited the file (eg. Adobe Camera Raw, Lightroom, Snapseed, Google, FFmpeg).
The original source/origin of the file content: 'camera', 'tiktok', 'whatsapp', or undefined.

Document-level information (PDF, Word, Excel, presentations, text, etc.).

Unlike `appDef` (the software that created the file), these fields describe
the document itself. `pageCount` handles both the PDF `PageCount` tag and
the Office `Pages` tag; `producer` is the PDF producer (when present).

Document-level information (PDF, Word, Excel, presentations, text, etc.).

Unlike `appDef` (the software that created the file), these fields describe
the document itself. `pageCount` handles both the PDF `PageCount` tag and
the Office `Pages` tag; `producer` is the PDF producer (when present).
Number of decimal places for seconds in DMS output. Default is 2.
Helper to format DMS strings for ExifTool writing
Parsed components of an exiftool date/time value.
e.g. "+02:00" (omitted when the value carries no timezone).
